notes: Partition verified: s001–s012 and t001–t014 each appear exactly once across the 13 units; every aligned unit has nonempty arrays with heads inside them, and the single added unit has an empty source and null source head.

t007 *that* is the one genuinely contested call and the accepted reading holds. The Greek result clause is asyndetic — no ὥστε or ὅτι stands in the verse — and rule 86's named licensors are a participle or a conjunction expressed elsewhere in the sentence, neither of which is present; a bare degree adverb already fully spent on *so* is not one. The competing discontinuous *so … that* frame on οὕτω under rule 15 is named in the unit note as rule 16 requires, so nothing further is owed.

s005/s006 split is correct. Rule 22's determiner clause yields to rule 32 where a participle follows, and rule 90 confines its one-word reading to pairs the ASV renders with a single English word; here two words stand, so the article keeps *the* under rule 19 and φανταζόμενον keeps *appearance*.

The ἔκφοβός … εἰμι … ἔντρομος recast is handled consistently. εἰμι is expressed, so no rule 53/63 supplied-copula question arises, and the only English left for it is the subject *I* its inflection supplies — rule 9's preference for the lexical verb cannot reach *fear* or *quake*, which answer to the two adjectives. Heads on *fear* and *quake* follow rule 91's operational test, this verse's own φοβερόν → *fearful* confirming where the φοβ- root's English sits, with *exceedingly* answering to the intensive ἐκ- prefix on the pattern rule 84 sets for an alpha-privative.
